projects.title: Live Holographic Video Streaming over 5G
projects.description: Building an end-to-end live holographic video conferencing testbed fusing 3 Intel RealSense depth cameras into a 3D point cloud at 10 fps over a private OpenAirInterface 5G standalone network to Unity/C#. Designed region-aware point cloud coding using PCA to prioritize facial details, raising head visual quality by 6.5 dB PSNR at the same network traffic. Deployed an offline reinforcement learning controller (Conservative Q-Learning) across 58 live sessions, which achieved a 1.38 fps higher frame rate and reduced time spent in the lowest-quality mode from 41.0% down to 9.3% compared to a conventional threshold-based controller.

projects.title: Semantic Mulsemedia Communication Framework
projects.institution: University of Nebraska-Lincoln (Funded by NASA Nebraska Space Grant & Layman Seed Award)
projects.description: Developed a novel cross-modal framework (CNN-LSTM sensor predictor + 3D conditional GAN video reconstructor) that transmits only one initial video frame alongside sensor measurements, cutting transmitted data by over 96%. Reconstructs high-fidelity video at the receiver even under severe wireless channel noise and poor signal conditions down to 3 dB signal-to-noise ratio.

publications.title: Cross-Modal Creation and Recovery for Semantic Mulsemedia Communication
publications.authors: Adhikari, A., Guo, H., and Akyildiz, I. F.
publications.conference: Proc. 24th IEEE/IFIP International Symposium on Modeling and Optimization in Mobile, Ad Hoc, and Wireless Networks (WiOpt)
publications.details: First author. Proposed a cross-modal semantic communication framework that transmits compact sensor measurements instead of streaming continuous raw video, cutting transmitted data by over 96%. A 3D-convolutional conditional GAN then reconstructs the missing video at the receiver, preserving high visual clarity (SSIM 0.83) even under severe wireless channel noise and degraded signal conditions (down to 3 dB signal-to-noise ratio). Research funded by the NASA Nebraska Space Grant and the Layman Seed Award.

publications.title: Region-Aware Adaptive Streaming for Holographic Video Conferencing
publications.authors: Adhikari, A., Sarpong, D. A., Bhusal, R., Guo, H., Wang, P., and Akyildiz, I. F.
publications.conference: Submitted to National Conference on Communications (NCC)
publications.details: First author. Addresses the massive bandwidth and computational bottlenecks of streaming live 3D human point clouds (>200 Mbps uncompressed) over dynamic 5G networks. Developed a region-aware coding scheme that segments the head from the body using PCA to prioritize facial details, improving visual quality by 6.5 dB PSNR without increasing network bandwidth. Formulated a full-system model capturing the interplay between point cloud processing and network limits, and implemented an offline Conservative Q-Learning (CQL) controller that delivers a 1.38 fps higher frame rate and reduces time spent in the lowest-quality representation from 41.0% to 9.3% compared to conventional threshold-based adaptation.
